_meta.source: Pakistani retailer listings (URLs and quotes on every item), the Honda generator owner's manual and published battery life ranges; no official price list exists
_meta.method: Equipment only, no installation. Low = lowest listed price, high = highest, over the publishers counted in n_sources; listings seen only in search snippets (W11stop returns HTTP 403) and clearly stale or out-of-range prices are not counted. No retailer page shows its own update date, so every price is 'live on the page on the checked date'. The UPS vs solar vs generator calculator (N7) uses the middle of each range. Batteries, hybrid inverters and panels come from data/component-prices.json and data/solar-prices.json, not from this file.
_meta.status: Secondary sources only; refresh monthly with data/component-prices.json.

tubular_unit.note: One tubular battery as priced in data/component-prices.json (12 V 180-220 Ah): 200 Ah is used for the bank count.

lithium_pack.note: Home LiFePO4 batteries are sold as whole packs; the 51.2 V 100 Ah pack priced in data/component-prices.json (item size given here) is used, so a small backup still buys one full pack.

battery_life_years.note: Tubular: published range 2 to 5 years in Pakistani use (AGS 3-5, Osaka 3-4, Phoenix 3-5; 2 to 3 years 'more common'); 3 years is used. LiFePO4: 2,500 to 6,000 cycles at 80% depth of discharge on manufacturer datasheets, one cycle a day; 8 years is used (below the cycle life, allowing for heat). Engineer to confirm both.

sources.quote: AGS 3–5 years, Osaka 3–4 years, Phoenix 3–5 years
